title: CSV Export Guard
summary: Previews what each column turns into when the CSV opens in a spreadsheet, so leading zeros, long IDs and dates aren't silently corrupted.
description: Previews how each column opens in a spreadsheet (phone numbers and PIN codes losing leading zeros or +, long IDs becoming 1.23457E+15, "3-4" turning into a date, cells starting with = + - @ running as formulas) and offers per-column fixes.
catches: Leading zeros and + signs dropped from phone numbers and codes
Long numeric IDs turned into scientific notation
Cells starting with = + - @ that run as formulas (CSV injection)
limits: Predicts typical Excel/Sheets behaviour; locale settings and other apps may differ
Forcing text or prefixing formulas changes the raw CSV, which other importers may not expect
Checks the rows you pass, not a whole export streamed from the server
a11y: Columns are a labelled list; fix toggles use aria-pressed
The "no problems" icon has an aria-label; arrows are aria-hidden
server: Neutralise formula-leading cells when generating CSV on the server as well, since exports can be produced without this component.
